request: What impact did passing Obamacare have on the federal budget?

reply.reply: The contemporary CBO/JCT estimate was that the Affordable Care Act would reduce federal deficits by **$210 billion** over FY2012–FY2021. This was a projection, not a measurement of the law’s actual eventual budget impact (CRS R41664, PDF p. 7). The estimate combined projected coverage-expansion costs of $1,390 billion with $348 billion in related offsets, while separate new revenues and direct-spending savings were projected at $1,252 billion (same citation). The sources reviewed do not establish what the ACA ultimately did to the federal budget. See the [brief](output/briefs/case-20261021-164502-c10d.html) for details.
reply.reasoning: Verified CRS material summarizes the February 2011 CBO/JCT baseline estimates, directly addressing the projected fiscal impact. It does not establish realized subsequent budget effects, so the answer is partial.
